comment: THE lesson catalog — single source of truth for nav, Lesson Center, audio, OG (epic wb-lplk). Tier 1 = the concepts; tier 2 = the constructs/primitives. status: live | planned. Sub-lessons nest under their parent and inherit its color.

sublessons.title: bundles
sublessons.dek: What a .wbundle actually is — a plain zip of workbook.html + workbook.org + vfs.sqlite + manifest.json — and the exact round trip: bundle, ship, unbundle, restore, with nothing proprietary in the container.

sublessons.title: nesting
sublessons.dek: Workbooks inside workbooks: the org tree makes every workbook a graftable subtree, nested workflows compile into one DAG of sub-worlds with typed imports/exports, and an upgrade gate keeps combining and removing safe.

sublessons.title: signatures
sublessons.dek: Make provenance travel with the bytes: sign a workbook with a self-certifying did:key (Ed25519 over canonical JSON, embedded in the file) and verify both the signature and that the artifact hasn't been touched since.

sublessons.title: specs
sublessons.dek: How a workbook identifies and describes itself from the inside — the inline org spec and embedded source markers that make the format filename-independent and self-explaining.

sublessons.title: git
sublessons.dek: The artifact is version control native: one file, real diffs, the whole project's history in the repo you already have.

sublessons.title: sharing
sublessons.dek: Hand a workbook to anyone with cryptographic identity attached: did:key signatures, single authentication, and what the recipient can verify without an account.

sublessons.title: the dock
sublessons.dek: The reader understands the Dock as a typed capability membrane: the host hands a workbook only the functions its grants permit, so a component asking for an ungranted power fails to even instantiate.

sublessons.title: capabilities
sublessons.dek: The reader can read and reason about a Policy profile: the four standard profiles, how each maps to a memory ceiling, a wall-clock CPU trap, and a capability list — and why a minimal profile literally has no network stack.

sublessons.title: sandboxes
sublessons.dek: The reader can trace a docked workbook through its whole state machine — created → active → suspended → frozen → archived — and sees why 'freeze' is just 'stop the process, keep the SQLite file', no VM snapshot needed.

sublessons.title: keepers
sublessons.dek: The reader learns how a workbook keeps working with nobody watching: keeper workers ticking agent defs on intervals, singleton vs crew scheduling, lifecycle specs that decide what each tick is, and schedules declared in the org source.

sublessons.title: planes
sublessons.dek: The reader understands why one Nexus runs two separate HTTP surfaces — an authed control plane and an anonymous GET-only content plane — and how a single BEAM node serves many custom domains via an ETS-backed SNI registry, no reverse proxy.

sublessons.title: deployments
sublessons.dek: The reader stands up a Nexus both ways — a cloud-identical krunvm microVM on their laptop and a Fly deploy — and understands deployment.org as inert declarative config where moving to the cloud is editing one property.

sublessons.title: telemetry
sublessons.dek: One event shape across the whole engine — what gets recorded, how agents and the autopoet read it, and why one grammar of signal beats a zoo of logs.

sublessons.title: gitops
sublessons.dek: The engine syncs to git: tenant repos, commits as the public changelog, and push-to-live publishing.

sublessons.title: hot swap
sublessons.dek: Loaded artifacts replace themselves live — a git change lands, the new toolkit/def swaps in, nothing reboots.

sublessons.title: networking
sublessons.dek: No ambient network, ever: how brokered TCP/UDP/TLS and engine-held HTTP give workbooks exactly the connections they were granted.

sublessons.title: imports
sublessons.dek: Anything → toolkit: how wbx toolkit import sniffs nine source shapes (Claude skills, MCP configs, OpenAPI specs, npm/pip CLIs, cursor rules, AGENTS.md…), mechanically translates docs to org, and scaffolds a real manifest + skill tree — with carried scripts honestly flagged as untrusted.

sublessons.title: audits
sublessons.dek: Ready, convertible, or blocked: how the static dependency audit classifies every carried script against the wasm lanes, writes findings INTO the toolkit's own manifest, and emits a checkbox fix-up plan an agent can work through to done — with --fix closing the loop as push → build → verify.

sublessons.title: lanes
sublessons.dek: The crux bet of the toolkit layer: C, Rust, Zig, Go, and JS compilers that are themselves compiled to WebAssembly, so untrusted source is built entirely inside the sandbox — c4, mrustc-to-C, zig1's C backend, yaegi interpretation, and QuickJS embedding, each a different trick to dodge native execution.

sublessons.title: promotion
sublessons.dek: Session → workspace → registry: an agent writes a source file, build-inline registers it as a command in one step, and promote materializes it as a real source-owned toolkit — org owns the spec, wasm owns the artifact, and self-authoring never widens granted capabilities.

sublessons.title: trust
sublessons.dek: What the signature actually binds: an Ed25519 did:key signature over the canonical manifest body ties the declared contract (EXEC/CAPS/BUILD_SRC) to an author identity, the build gate refuses any unsigned or tampered third-party toolkit, and the sandbox bounds damage regardless — two layers, distinct jobs.

sublessons.title: verification
sublessons.dek: Verify and eval as the toolkit's quality gates: structural checks (manifest, skills, exec, caps, provenance), then bundled evals/*.org cases where an agent is run against a :TASK: with the toolkit's own manual injected and a judge model scores the result and tool trace against a :RUBRIC:.

sublessons.title: syntax
sublessons.dek: Learn the whole grammar in one sitting — headlines, tags, TODO states, drawers, timestamps, source blocks — by drilling each construct against the kernel's actual parse output, with side-by-side markdown comparisons showing exactly what structure markdown throws away.

sublessons.title: tangling
sublessons.dek: Literate programming, weaponized: how source blocks plus six header args (:deps :uses :in :out :persist :dir) compile a document into a WIT-world-shaped build plan — components, capability imports, and a DAG of :out→:in edges.

sublessons.title: drawers
sublessons.dek: How :PROPERTIES: drawers turn a headline into a typed record — the key-value mechanism behind toolkit manifests, agent identities, and the spec block inside every learn page.

sublessons.title: timestamps
sublessons.dek: The full date grammar — active <…> vs inactive […], SCHEDULED vs DEADLINE, +1d/.+/++ repeaters, and the :SCHEDULE: cron escape hatch — and how a timestamp on a headline becomes a workflow that actually runs every morning.

sublessons.title: the kernel
sublessons.dek: Inside OQL — one 550-line pure Rust crate (parse, tangle, validate, render on orgize) that ships as three surfaces from the same source: a native rlib in the wb CLI, a WIT-typed wasm Component in the runtime and desktop, and a raw ptr/len build running in this very website.

sublessons.title: to-dos
sublessons.dek: The TODO grammar in full: states, transitions, what DONE actually records, and how state changes become history.

sublessons.title: tags
sublessons.dek: Tags as structure: categorize headlines, drive queries, and carry meaning machines can filter on.

sublessons.title: loops
sublessons.dek: What a single agent run actually is — the model→tools→append cycle, why every tool call is wall-clock bounded, and how a run leaves a fully readable trace.

sublessons.title: authoring
sublessons.dek: Write a complete agent definition in plain org — the :agent: node, the system-prompt heading, declared toolkits — and understand exactly how the runtime parses and runs it.

sublessons.title: context repo
sublessons.dek: An agent's memory is a workbook — a git repo of plain files it reads, writes, and commits — not a vector store bolted on the side; the board, the canon, and the logs all live in one place anyone can diff.

sublessons.title: spawning
sublessons.dek: How a run comes to exist and stays alive — supervised sessions you start with one call, then poll or stream while the agent works for minutes, surviving the caller that launched it.

sublessons.title: orchestration
sublessons.dek: How standing agents keep a cadence — the keeper's tick, a lifecycle state machine declared in org, and a crew of workers sharing one board with claims as protocol, not locks.

sublessons.title: human in the loop
sublessons.dek: Insert a real human checkpoint into a live run — a review canvas the agent opens, a commit the human makes, and a FIFO the agent polls mid-loop to pick the verdict up.

sublessons.title: runtime config
sublessons.dek: Every knob that shapes an agent without touching engine code — the env contract, org manifests, model and toolkit props, intervals, and the exec trust grant.

sublessons.title: dreaming
sublessons.dek: What an agent does between runs — a sleep phase that digests telemetry, commits, and the backlog into a dream journal whose verdicts mechanically steer the next waking run.

sublessons.title: evals
sublessons.dek: Judge agent output systematically: briefs in, judged runs out — the evaluation bench as a standing practice.

sublessons.title: modes
sublessons.dek: How one binary serves two audiences — TTY detection, the --agent/--json switches, the {ok, verb, data, error} envelope, and the stable exit-code map an agent can branch on without parsing prose.

sublessons.title: pipelines
sublessons.dek: Build real pipelines with the kernel verbs — query, tangle, and lint accept '-' for stdin, emit JSON, and compose with --json and jq so generated org never touches a temp file.

sublessons.title: doctor
sublessons.dek: Wire wbx into your shell and let it check itself — doctor's report-not-judge contract (always exit 0, JSON for agents), the bare-wbx where-am-I landing, clap-generated completions, and upgrade's npm-aware self-update.

sublessons.title: deploy kit
sublessons.dek: Stand up an engine with the deploy-kit — scaffold deployment.org with init, validate, apply, and watch one verb set converge a local container or a cloud provider, with secrets declared by name and never written into the artifact.

sublessons.title: the seam
sublessons.dek: Why the same crate compiles to your laptop and into the engine's sandbox — one Io trait (http/read/write/spawn) as the only place the two targets differ, native std/reqwest on one side, Dock-brokered host imports on the other, plus engine discovery via runtime.json.

sublessons.title: validations
sublessons.dek: DONE is a claim until a check proves it — the three-rung ladder of plan validation (dangling inputs, missing langs), task acceptance (:done-when: and :check blocks run fail-closed in the WASM shell), and build conformance, which together turn drift from a shrug into a named diagnostic.

sublessons.title: schedules
sublessons.dek: The full grammar of time in a plan — active vs inactive timestamps, +1w/.+/++ repeaters, the :SCHEDULE: cron property — and the keeper, the engine that actually fires them: workers, crews, lifecycle specs, and the breather between ticks.

sublessons.title: boards
sublessons.dek: Why there is no board model anywhere in the runtime — a board is the kernel's render() over the plan file plus a write path back into it, and any surface (kanban, status page, an agent's ready list) is the same one-file two-way binding.

sublessons.title: waves
sublessons.dek: How a compiled world executes — topological waves where every step whose predecessors are done runs in parallel, producers' stdout piped into consumers' stdin along the edges, and agent-lang components fanning out sub-agents inside the same DAG.

sublessons.title: worlds
sublessons.dek: What tangle_plan actually computes — edges inferred by matching :out to :in, exports as the outputs nobody consumed, imports from :uses, nested workflows as sub-worlds — and why the result is shaped like a WIT world on purpose.

sublessons.title: upgrades
sublessons.dek: How a live plan changes safely — the Motoko/Candid-style subtyping rules (exports may grow but never shrink, imports may shrink but never grow, an output type may never change) that let the kernel refuse a breaking redeploy before it runs.

sublessons.title: queries
sublessons.dek: How to actually query the disk: the vfs table's real schema, the Policy-gated vfs-query Dock import your component calls, error-as-JSON safety so a bad query can never crash the engine, and one SQL statement run across a whole library of workbooks.

sublessons.title: volumes
sublessons.dek: The disk isn't one undifferentiated tree — it's three named regions (workspace, memory, tmp) with different lifetimes, and knowing which one a byte lives in tells you whether it persists, travels, or evaporates.

sublessons.title: sync
sublessons.dek: What 'the disk gets a heartbeat' actually means: the instance lifecycle state machine, freeze/resume as a file copy instead of a VM snapshot, WAL-mode streaming to off-box replicas, and clone-per-tenant so a thousand users each get their own copy of one template disk.

sublessons.title: privacy
sublessons.dek: Sharing exposes the work, never the session that produced it — one boundary module decides what leaves on every egress path (bundle, git, library), so agent memory, scratch files, and telemetry stay home unless the owner explicitly opts in.

sublessons.title: sealed sections
sublessons.dek: How part of a shipped disk can be ciphertext to everyone and plaintext to the right person: AES-256-GCM envelopes whose content keys never ride in the bundle — they're escrowed at the runtime, released only after a posture check, and optionally wrapped to a recipient's DID so there's no plaintext-key honeypot anywhere.

sublessons.title: foreign tables
sublessons.dek: Make FROM reach past the file: register a data-source plugin and a query against its entity routes to a live API instead of the local store — or run the sync daemon and keep a resident, queryable, agent-airgapped mirror of the outside world inside the disk.
